chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: A man marries for mut'ah (temporary marriage) for a year, or less, or more. He said: 'When there is something known to a known term.' I said: And it becomes clear/permanent without divorce? He said: 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for temporary marriage (mut'ah) to become permanent in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the condition of a known duration ('ajal ma'lum) is reaffirmed as the essential pillar of temporary marriage (Nikah al-Mut'ah). The Imam clarifies that 'tabayyun' (becoming clear/permanent) occurs without the need for a formal divorce pronouncement, highlighting a distinct legal mechanism in Shia jurisprudence where the marriage status transforms or concludes based on the fulfillment of the agreed term or cohabitation, distinguishing it from permanent marriage which requires explicit talaq.
